_about: Single source of truth for texture import settings per asset folder (build-size budget, docs/build_size.md). First matching rule wins. `apply_import_rules.js` rewrites the [params] of existing .import files; the import scripts call it after importing so new assets get the folder's settings. `size_limit` is Godot's own import-time downscale (max dimension in px): the full-size source stays in the project and only the packed texture shrinks, so raising a limit later re-exports at higher quality. mode: 0 lossless, 1 lossy WebP, 2 VRAM compressed (BC7 when hq). `lossy_over_px`: the lossy mode applies only to images whose longest side exceeds it (small UI pieces and icons stay lossless).

rules.why: normal (RG) + roughness (B): must stay RGB, so not the normal-map mode; half the colour texture's size
kit building, prop and sign surfaces

painted world sprites: lossy keeps the alpha edge lossless and transparent space costs almost nothing; NOT downscaled (head anchors, pivots and hat fits are in canvas pixels, see world/sprites/sprite_anchors.gd) and not trimmed or atlased for the same reason
card art; drawn at most 300x450 px at 1080p
dialogue and vendor portraits (up to ~970 px tall in vendor stages)
